reason: The text describes the Israelites being oppressed by external enemies (the Canaanite king Jabin and commander Sisera) and crying out to God (אֶל־ יְהוָה) for deliverance, not complaining against their own leaders. The narrative presents Deborah as a prophetess and judge, and Barak as a military commander, both of whom are positioned as instruments of divine salvation. There is no expression of complaint or dissatisfaction directed toward these leaders. The text follows the typical Judges cycle pattern: Israel does evil, God allows oppression, Israel cries to God, and God raises up a deliverer—but this is not a narrative of the people voicing complaints about their leadership.
